builder_plan.scenario: Start with one repeated product task that has a measurable failure or cost.
builder_plan.change: Read the methods and identify one change you can isolate in that workflow.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current implementation on the same held-out tasks.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful outcomes, response time, human rework, and total cost per successful task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Coordinate Basis Linear Bandits with Sublinear Regret over Low-Rank Clusters
summary: CBL replaces full O(d^2) covariance updates and fixed-rank sketched approximations (e.g., SOFUL) in high-dimensional linear bandits with clustered exact-orthonormal-basis representations plus sentinel-based cluster switching. It costs the bookkeeping of multiple clusters, per-cluster bases, and a tunable rank bound l, with per-round cost O(r_bar^2) instead of O(d^2). It can fail to deliver savings if the data has high intrinsic rank, clusters are poorly formed, or the workload is not an online bandit problem at all, in which case the machinery yields no benefit.
rationale: The method is only relevant if the reader operates a high-dimensional linear contextual bandit system in production; it does not apply to LLM inference, training, or API-based deployment workloads.

claims.statement: CBL replaces full O(d^2) covariance updates and fixed-rank sketched approximations (e.g., SOFUL) in high-dimensional linear bandits with clustered exact-orthonormal-basis representations plus sentinel-based cluster switching. It costs the bookkeeping of multiple clusters, per-cluster bases, and a tunable rank bound l, with per-round cost O(r_bar^2) instead of O(d^2). It can fail to deliver savings if the data has high intrinsic rank, clusters are poorly formed, or the workload is not an online bandit problem at all, in which case the machinery yields no benefit.

Reduces per-round update computation from O(d^2) to O(r_bar^2), where r_bar = min(r, l) is the effective cluster dimension, while guaranteeing sublinear regret without the spectral-tail vulnerability of fixed-rank sketching methods such as SOFUL.
